decisions.choice: the narrator sums up Jesus's public ministry: many signs, and still unbelief
decisions.reason: Jesus has just left the crowd and hidden himself (12:36). The narrator now looks back over all the signs Jesus did in public, from the wine at Cana (2:11) to the raising of Lazarus (11:43-44), and states the result: the people as a whole did not believe. 1:11 said it in advance ("his own people did not receive him"), and 20:30-31 says the signs were written so that readers may believe. With 12:44-50 this closes the account of Jesus's public ministry; from 13:1 he speaks to his disciples alone.

decisions.choice: though he had done ...: they kept on not believing
alternatives: because he had done so many signs
decisions.reason: The opening phrase gives the circumstances, and set against "they did not believe" it means "although". The verb "were believing" is in a tense of ongoing action: it describes a settled refusal, not a single moment. "They" are the people who saw the signs, the crowd of 12:29-34 and the people as a whole, not every person (12:42 says that many believed).

decisions.choice: so that ... might be fulfilled: their unbelief was what Scripture had foretold, and so part of God's purpose
alternatives: God made them disbelieve for the sole reason that a prophecy had to come true
"so that" weakened to "with the result that"
decisions.reason: This is the first time John uses the formula "so that the Scripture might be fulfilled" (also 13:18; 15:25; 17:12; 19:24, 36). The words "so that" keep their sense of purpose: what happened was not outside God's plan, and Isaiah had spoken of it long before. But the formula does not say that the prophecy forced anyone to disbelieve. The sentence itself blames the unbelief on the people, who refused after seeing so many signs (12:37), and 12:43 gives a human reason, love for the glory that people give. 12:39-40 takes the question further.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 53:1, as it reads in the Greek of Isaiah
decisions.reason: The words match the Greek translation of Isaiah 53:1 exactly. That translation begins with "Lord", which the Hebrew does not have. The verse opens Isaiah's song about the servant of the LORD who is lifted up and glorified (52:13) and yet despised and rejected (53:3). "Who has believed?" expects the answer "hardly anyone". John sees in it the response to Jesus; Paul quotes the same verse of the response to the gospel (Romans 10:16).

decisions.choice: report: the message that was heard
decisions.reason: The word means what is heard, so here the message announced. "Our message" is what the prophet, and in John's use Jesus and those who speak for him, have proclaimed. The address "Lord" at the start is to God.

decisions.choice: Jesus (for "he"); It happened this way so that (B), This happened so that (R)
alternatives: so that (joined to the sentence before)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the last person named is Isaiah in the next clause and the scene before is a crowd. They start a new sentence for the purpose clause, so they supply its subject. Readable says "the people" for "them" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: our message (B), the message we brought (R); come true (R)
decisions.reason: "Report" now suggests a written document. "Message" is the plain sense (meaning decision m5). Readable says "come true" for "be fulfilled".

decisions.choice: anuncio (L); mensaje (B); el mensaje que trajimos (R)
decisions.reason: The message that was heard (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); the imperfect "croyaient" for the settled refusal (L, R); speech and quotations keep their own tenses
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (12:37-50). The narrator's summary uses the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("prononça", "crurent") and the passé composé at Readable ("C’est arrivé"), as French narrative and school reading do. Literal and Readable keep the imperfect "ils ne croyaient pas" for the Greek tense of ongoing action (meaning decision m2); Balanced sums it up with "ils ne crurent pas", as the English "did not believe" does. Jesus's words in 12:44-50 use the passé composé ("je suis venu", "j’ai prononcée").

decisions.choice: notre annonce (L); notre message (B); le message que nous avons apporté (R)
alternatives: ce que nous avons fait entendre
decisions.reason: The word means what is heard, the message proclaimed (meaning decision m5). "Prédication" sounds like a sermon in church; Literal says "annonce", the act of making it known, and Balanced and Readable the plain "message".

decisions.choice: "điều chúng tôi rao báo" (L); "sứ điệp" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the message that was heard; "sứ điệp" is the usual modern word for a message from God.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect for Jesus is carried by the honorific -si- and 께서 at every level (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: 예언자 for "prophet"
decisions.reason: 예언자 is the current standard word; 선지자 is the older church term that many Protestant readers know, and a reviewer may prefer it.

decisions.choice: o nosso anúncio (L); a nossa mensagem (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means what was heard, the message announced (meaning decision m5). Literal says "anúncio", a message proclaimed; Balanced and Readable say "mensagem", as the English does.

pt.B: E a quem foi revelado o braço do Senhor?"
pt.R: E a quem o Senhor mostrou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} poder?"

decisions.choice: the arm of the Lord: God's power at work, above all to rescue his people
decisions.reason: In Scripture God's arm is his strength in action: he brought Israel out of Egypt "with an outstretched arm" (Exodus 6:6), and Isaiah calls on the arm of the LORD to wake and act (Isaiah 51:9) and says that he has bared his holy arm before the nations (Isaiah 52:10). John applies the line to Jesus's signs: God's power was shown openly, and still few saw it for what it was.

decisions.choice: Lord: in Isaiah 53:1 this stands for God's own name, the LORD
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Isaiah 53:1 the word is the divine name; the Greek of Isaiah, which John quotes, has "Lord". As at 1:23, the Gospel uses for the work of Jesus a verse about the LORD himself.

decisions.choice: to whom has it been revealed?: hardly anyone has seen it; God is the one who reveals
decisions.reason: The passive "has been revealed" leaves God as the one who makes known, and the question, like the first half of the verse, expects the answer "to very few". The second line repeats the first in other words, as Hebrew poetry does.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: As at 1:23: the style guide keeps "the LORD" for the divine name in the Old Testament itself. Here the Gospel quotes the verse with the Greek word for "Lord"; meaning decision m2 says whom it means.

decisions.choice: the Lord shown his power
alternatives: the arm of the Lord been revealed
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the picture (meaning decision m1) in plain words. Literal and Balanced keep "the arm of the Lord", a phrase Scripture uses often.

decisions.choice: el Señor
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 53:1 this stands for God's own name (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: ha mostrado el Señor su poder
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: à qui le Seigneur a-t-il révélé son bras ? (B)
alternatives: à qui le bras du Seigneur a-t-il été révélé ?
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God as the one who reveals (meaning decision m3). Balanced makes that plain with an active verb and "son bras", which takes the deity pronoun setting; Literal keeps the passive and the Greek order, with "le bras" placed first.

decisions.choice: The prophet speaks to the Lord in the formal polite style (합쇼체)
decisions.reason: A prayer addressed to God takes 합쇼체, as Jesus's prayers to the Father do in this guide.

pt.R: Eles não podiam acreditar por causa do que Isaías disse em outro lugar:

decisions.choice: for this reason ... because: the reason is the one given next, in Isaiah's words
alternatives: for this reason: pointing back to the fulfillment of 12:38
decisions.reason: In John "for this reason" followed by "because" usually points forward to the reason that follows (5:16, 18; 8:47; 10:17). So the reason they could not believe is what Isaiah said in 6:10. The phrase could also point back to 12:38; either way, Isaiah's words are the explanation.

decisions.choice: could not believe: John holds together human refusal and God's judgment, without saying how they fit
alternatives: God had decided beforehand that they would never believe, whatever they did
decisions.reason: 12:37 says they did not believe; this verse says they could not. John states both and does not explain how they fit. Isaiah 6:9-10 announced a hardening as God's judgment on a people who had long refused to listen (Isaiah 1:2-4; 5:1-7), and in John too it comes after many signs were seen and rejected (12:37). Jesus had said the same: "you cannot hear my word" (8:43), and "how can you believe, when you receive glory from one another?" (5:44). The text does not say that any person who wanted to believe was prevented: the next verse but one says that many believed (12:42), and Jesus goes on calling people to believe (12:44-46).

decisions.choice: again: in another passage
alternatives: Isaiah said it a second time
decisions.reason: "Again" introduces a second quotation, as in 19:37, not a repeated saying of Isaiah.

decisions.choice: in another place
decisions.reason: "Isaiah said again" could suggest he said the same thing twice. Balanced and Readable give the sense (meaning decision m3). Readable puts the sentence as "the reason ... is", which says plainly that the reason follows (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: en otro lugar
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m3).

records.literal_gloss: "He has blinded of them the eyes and he hardened of them the heart, so that not they might see with the eyes and understand with the heart and turn, and I will heal them."

en.L: "He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they would not see with [their] eyes and understand with [their] heart and turn, and I will heal them."
en.B: "He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they would not see with their eyes, and understand with their heart, and turn, and I would heal them."
en.R: "He has blinded their eyes and made their hearts hard. He did this so that they would not see with their eyes or understand with their hearts. Otherwise they would turn back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I would heal them."

es.L: «Ha cegado sus ojos y endurecido su corazón, para que no vean con los ojos y entiendan con el corazón y se vuelvan, y yo los sanaré».

vi.B: "Ngài đã làm mù mắt họ và làm cứng lòng họ, để họ không thấy bằng mắt, không hiểu bằng lòng, và không quay lại để {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chữa lành họ."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 6:10, quoted freely
decisions.reason: John's form of the verse matches neither the Hebrew nor the Greek of Isaiah word for word. In the Hebrew, God tells the prophet to make the people's heart dull and shut their eyes; in the Greek, the people's heart has grown dull and they have shut their eyes. John has "he has blinded ... and hardened", speaks of eyes and heart, and leaves out the ears. The verse comes from Isaiah's call, after he saw the Lord on his throne (Isaiah 6:1-9). The same passage is quoted in Matthew 13:14-15, Mark 4:12 and Acts 28:26-27, always of people who hear God's message and refuse it.

decisions.choice: he: God
decisions.reason: No subject is named. In Isaiah 6 it is God who sends the prophet with this message, and the "I" who would heal is God, so "he" is most naturally God as well. It cannot easily be Jesus, who in John gives sight to the blind (9:39) and is the one in whom they fail to believe. Paul says that "the god of this age" has blinded unbelievers' minds (2 Corinthians 4:4), so some take "he" to be the devil; but nothing in this passage points to him.

decisions.choice: and I will heal them: still part of what is prevented, "or else they would turn and I would heal them"
alternatives: a promise: "and yet I will heal them"
decisions.reason: "I will heal" is a future that continues the clause beginning "so that ... not": the blinding keeps them from seeing, understanding, turning, and being healed. The speaker is God, as in Isaiah, where the words come from the voice of the Lord (Isaiah 6:8). Healing means being made whole again by God, as in Isaiah 53:5.

decisions.choice: heart: mind and will; hardened: made dull and unresponsive; turn: turn back to God
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is where a person thinks and decides, so to "understand with the heart" is to grasp and take in. The verb "hardened" is used of minds that cannot take in what they see (Mark 6:52; 8:17). "Turn" is the Old Testament word for turning back to God. On how this judgment and the people's own refusal belong together, see the note at 12:39.

decisions.choice: made their hearts hard; He did this so that; Otherwise they would turn back to me
alternatives: hardened their heart, so that they would not ... turn, and I would heal them
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long sentence and spells out what the turning would lead to (meaning decision m3), and adds "to me", since the turning is to God, the speaker (meaning decision m4). "Me" here is God speaking in Isaiah's words, so it takes the deity pronoun setting. Literal and Balanced keep the collective singular "heart"; Readable says "hearts".

decisions.choice: Ha cegado, with no pronoun
decisions.reason: Spanish, like Greek, carries the subject (God, meaning decision m2) in the verb. Readable starts with "Él", which, as the first word of a sentence, takes no setting.

decisions.choice: Lo hizo para que; De lo contrario, se volverían a mí

decisions.reason: "I will heal them" carries on the clause of what is prevented (meaning decision m3). "Revenir" gives the sense of turning back to God (m4) without the church word "se convertir".

decisions.choice: "He" left unstated, with the honorific -si- (멀게 하셨고, 굳게 하셨다)

decisions.choice: because
decisions.reason: The two Greek words differ by one letter. The SBLGNT reads "because", which is found in the oldest papyri and the great early copies; many later manuscripts read "when" ("Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory"), which may have come from thinking of the time of Isaiah's vision. With "because", the vision is the reason Isaiah could speak of Christ. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: his glory: the glory of Jesus, the Son
alternatives: the glory of God the Father, with Isaiah speaking of Christ only in the words of 53:1
decisions.reason: "Him" in 12:37 and 12:42 is Jesus ("they did not believe in him", "they believed in him"), so the same word here is most naturally Jesus as well. In Isaiah 6:1-5 the prophet saw the Lord on a high throne and said, "my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts". John says that the glory Isaiah saw was the glory of the Son, who was with God in the beginning (1:1), whose glory was seen when he became flesh (1:14), and who had glory with the Father before the world existed (17:5); compare Abraham, who saw Jesus's day (8:56). The other view is noted in the footnote.

decisions.choice: these things: both quotations; spoke about him: Isaiah's words concerned Jesus
decisions.reason: "These things" covers what Isaiah says in 12:38 and 12:40. "Glory" here is God's own splendor, seen in a vision; in the next verse the same word is used of the glory people give one another (12:43).

decisions.choice: the glory of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, as meaning decision m2 reads the verse, since "he ... his ... him" would leave young readers unsure whom it means. Literal and Balanced keep "his", with the footnote.

decisions.choice: la gloria de Jesús
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: the rulers: members of the ruling council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word is used of Nicodemus, "a ruler of the Jews" (3:1), and of the authorities the crowd speaks of in 7:26. In 7:48 the Pharisees asked scornfully whether any of the rulers had believed in Jesus; here the narrator says that many had. Nicodemus (19:39) and Joseph of Arimathea, a disciple "but secretly, for fear of the Jews" (19:38), are examples.

decisions.choice: nevertheless: against the general unbelief of 12:37-40; were not confessing: their faith stayed hidden
decisions.reason: The two opening words together make a strong "even so": the hardening of 12:40 was not total. "They were not confessing" is ongoing: they kept their belief to themselves and did not say openly what they believed about Jesus, as in 9:22 ("if anyone confessed him to be the Christ").

decisions.choice: put out of the synagogue: shut out of the community's worship and common life
decisions.reason: The same word as 9:22 (see the note there) and 16:2. To be put out of the synagogue was to be cut off from one's own people. Here the threat comes "because of the Pharisees", who held great influence among the rulers (7:47-48).

decisions.choice: glory: here honor and approval, what one is worth in another's eyes
decisions.reason: The word means both splendor and honor. In 12:41 Isaiah saw Christ's glory; here the rulers prefer the honor that people give to the honor that God gives. John plays on the two senses, as in 5:41-44 ("how can you believe, when you receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?") and 7:18. Keeping the same word keeps the link with 12:41.

decisions.choice: the glory of people ... of God: the glory people give, and the glory God gives
decisions.reason: Set against "the glory of people", which can only mean the approval people give, "the glory of God" is the approval that comes from God, as in 5:44. It could be read as God's own glory, but the comparison points to where each kind of honor comes from.

decisions.choice: the glory that people give ... that God gives (B), that comes from God (R)
alternatives: the glory of people ... the glory of God (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where each glory comes from (meaning decision m5), keeping the key word "glory" (meaning decision m4). The Greek word for "people" means human beings in general, so it takes the gender setting at every level.

decisions.choice: would not say so openly (B), were afraid of ... did not tell anyone (R); expelled (B), thrown out (R)
decisions.reason: Gives the sense of "confess" here (meaning decision m2). Readable says "afraid of the Pharisees", which "because of the Pharisees" plainly implies. "Expelled" and "thrown out of the synagogue" are the wording used at 9:22. Readable says "leaders" for "rulers" and names Jesus for "him".

decisions.choice: {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: People in general, as at 5:41: inclusive default, traditional one tap away. The span takes in the verb where the subject changes number.

decisions.choice: no lo decían abiertamente (B); no se lo decían a nadie (R); expulsados
decisions.reason: As in English; "expulsado de la sinagoga" as at 9:22.

decisions.choice: la gloire (every level), with "que donnent les humains" / "que Dieu donne" (B, R)
decisions.reason: John plays on the two senses of the word, the glory Isaiah saw (12:41) and the honor people give (meaning decision m4). French "gloire" carries both, so the key word stays; Balanced and Readable say where each glory comes from (m5), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "nhà hội" for synagogue
decisions.reason: The established Protestant word; "hội đường" is the Catholic one and is listed for a reviewer. Settled for the whole Bible: Vietnamese follows the Protestant tradition's names and terms (the founder's decision, October 2026; docs/vietnamese-style.md).

decisions.choice: "loài người" / "người ta", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese words for people are already inclusive, so the English "people/men" setting has nothing to choose between; the same holds for "người ấy" in verses 47-48.

decisions.choice: 사람 / 사람들, with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean 사람 already means people of either sex, so the English gender setting has nothing to change here or in verses 47-48, where Korean says 그 사람 / 그들 without a gendered pronoun (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: 지도자들 for "the rulers"
decisions.reason: A plain word for the men of the ruling council that fits every level; the meaning decision says who they were.

decisions.choice: os governantes (L); as autoridades (B); os líderes (R)
decisions.reason: The rulers are members of the ruling council in Jerusalem (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the word used for the ruler in 12:31; Balanced and Readable say who they were in present-day words.

en.L: But Jesus cried out and said, "The one who believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} does not believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} but in the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \v 45 and the one who sees {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sees the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Then Jesus called out, "Anyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} believes not just in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but in the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 45 And anyone who sees {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sees the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Jesus called out loudly, "When people believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they are not only believing in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They are believing in the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \v 45 And when people see {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, they are seeing the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Pero Jesús clamó y dijo: «El que cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, no cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, sino en el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió; \v 45 y el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ve, ve al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió.
es.B: Entonces Jesús dijo en voz alta: «El que cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no cree solo en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, sino en el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió. \v 45 Y el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ve, ve al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió.
es.R: Jesús dijo en voz muy alta: «Cuando alguien cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, no está creyendo solo en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Está creyendo en el que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió. \v 45 Y cuando alguien {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ve, está viendo al que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió.

fr.L: Mais Jésus s’écria et dit : « Celui qui croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne croit pas en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, mais en celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé, \v 45 et celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} voit, voit celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
fr.B: Jésus dit alors d’une voix forte : « Celui qui croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne croit pas seulement en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, mais en celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. \v 45 Et celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} voit, voit celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.
fr.R: Jésus a dit très fort : « Quand quelqu’un croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, il ne croit pas seulement en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Il croit en celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. \v 45 Et quand quelqu’un {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} voit, il voit celui qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu akapaza sauti, akasema, "Anayeniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} haniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, bali yule aliyenituma, \v 45 na anayeniona {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} anamwona yule aliyenituma.
sw.B: Kisha Yesu akapaza sauti, "Yeyote anayeniamini haniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} tu, bali anamwamini yule aliyenituma. \v 45 Na yeyote anayeniona {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} anamwona yule aliyenituma.
sw.R: Yesu akapaza sauti kwa nguvu, "Watu wanaponiamini, hawaniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} tu. Wanamwamini yule aliyenituma. \v 45 Na watu wanaponiona, wanamwona yule aliyenituma.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu kêu lớn và nói: "Người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không phải tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, mà tin vào Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \v 45 và người thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là thấy Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đức Giê-xu lớn tiếng nói: "Ai tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không chỉ tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, mà còn tin vào Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \v 45 Và ai thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là thấy Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu lớn tiếng nói: "Khi người ta tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, họ không chỉ tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Họ đang tin vào Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \v 45 Và khi người ta thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, họ đang thấy Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그런데 예수께서 외쳐 말씀하셨다. "나를 믿는 사람은 나를 믿는 것이 아니라 나를 보내신 분을 믿는 것이다. \v 45 그리고 나를 보는 사람은 나를 보내신 분을 보는 것이다.
ko.B: 그때 예수께서 큰 소리로 말씀하셨다. "나를 믿는 사람은 나만 믿는 것이 아니라 나를 보내신 분을 믿는 것이다. \v 45 그리고 나를 보는 사람은 나를 보내신 분을 보는 것이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 큰 소리로 외치셨다. "사람들이 나를 믿으면, 나만 믿는 것이 아니다. 나를 보내신 분을 믿는 것이다. \v 45 그리고 사람들이 나를 보면, 나를 보내신 분을 보는 것이다.

pt.L: Mas Jesus clamou e disse: "Quem crê em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não crê em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, mas naquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou, \v 45 e quem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} vê vê aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou.
pt.B: Então Jesus falou em alta voz: "Quem crê em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não crê apenas em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, mas naquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou. \v 45 E quem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} vê está vendo aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou.
pt.R: Jesus falou bem alto: "Quando as pessoas acreditam em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, não estão acreditando só em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. Estão acreditando naquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou. \v 45 E, quando as pessoas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} veem, estão vendo aquele que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou.

decisions.choice: no time or place: a summary of Jesus's public message, his last words to the crowds
alternatives: a new speech given on a later occasion, after he came out of hiding
decisions.reason: In 12:36 Jesus went away and hid from the crowd, and nothing is said of his coming back. The narrator gives no setting here, only "Jesus cried out", the verb used for his public proclamations in the temple (7:28, 37). These verses gather what he has said throughout: believing in him is believing in the one who sent him (5:24), he is the light of the world (8:12), he came to save and not to condemn (3:17), and he speaks what the Father gives him (8:26-28). They are the last words of his public ministry in John; from 13:1 he speaks to his disciples.

decisions.choice: does not believe in me but in the one who sent me: not in me only, but in the Father through me
alternatives: faith in Jesus stops short of God
Jesus is not to be believed in at all
decisions.reason: "Not A but B" is a Hebrew way of saying "not so much A as B": Jesus has just called people to believe in him (12:36), so he is not turning faith away from himself but saying where it reaches. Mark 9:37 has the same form: "whoever receives me receives not me but the one who sent me".

decisions.choice: sees: perceives who he is
decisions.reason: The verb is used of seeing that takes in what is seen (6:40). To see Jesus in this way is to see the Father, as 14:9 says ("whoever has seen me has seen the Father"); no one has ever seen God, but the Son has made him known (1:18).

decisions.choice: the one who sent me: the Father, whose envoy Jesus is
decisions.reason: In Jewish practice, as across the ancient world, an envoy stood for the one who sent him, so that to receive or reject him was to receive or reject his sender (13:20; Luke 10:16). Jesus applies this to himself and the Father (5:23).

decisions.choice: believes not just in me (B); not only ... They are believing (R)
alternatives: does not believe in me but in the one who sent me (Literal)
decisions.reason: "Does not believe in me" would sound like a denial in English. Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (meaning decision m2); Literal keeps the Greek form.

decisions.choice: called out (B), called out loudly (R); Anyone who (B), When people (R)
decisions.reason: "Cried out" can suggest weeping; the verb means to speak out loudly in public. "Anyone who" and "people" keep the general sense without he or she.

decisions.choice: solo
decisions.reason: As in English: not in me only (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "Đấng đã sai Ta" for the Father who sent Jesus
decisions.reason: "Đấng" is the respectful classifier for God; it is used every time Jesus speaks of the one who sent him.

source.text: ἐγὼ φῶς εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐλήλυθα, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ μὴ μείνῃ.

records.literal_gloss: I light into the world have come, so that everyone the believing in me in the darkness not may remain.

en.L: I have come into the world [as] light, so that everyone who believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} may not remain in the darkness.
en.B: I have come as a light into the world, so that whoever believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will not remain in the darkness.
en.R: I have come into the world as a light. I came so that people who believe in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will not stay in the dark.

es.L: Yo he venido al mundo [como] luz, para que todo el que cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no permanezca en la oscuridad.
es.B: Yo he venido al mundo como luz, para que todo el que crea en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no se quede en la oscuridad.
es.R: Yo he venido al mundo como luz. Vine para que los que creen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no se queden en la oscuridad.

fr.L: Moi, je suis venu dans le monde [comme] lumière, afin que quiconque croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne demeure pas dans les ténèbres.
fr.B: Je suis venu dans le monde comme une lumière, pour que quiconque croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne demeure pas dans les ténèbres.
fr.R: Je suis venu dans le monde comme une lumière. Je suis venu pour que les gens qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ne restent pas dans l’obscurité.

sw.L: Mimi nimekuja ulimwenguni [kama] nuru, ili kila anayeniamini asikae gizani.
sw.B: Nimekuja ulimwenguni kama nuru, ili yeyote anayeniamini asikae gizani.
sw.R: Nimekuja ulimwenguni kama nuru. Nilikuja ili watu wanaoniamini wasibaki gizani.

vi.L: Ta đã đến thế gian [làm] ánh sáng, để mọi người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không ở lại trong bóng tối.
vi.B: Ta đã đến thế gian như ánh sáng, để ai tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì không ở lại trong bóng tối.
vi.R: Ta đã đến thế gian như một ánh sáng. Ta đến để những ai tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không còn ở trong bóng tối.

ko.L: 나는 빛으로 세상에 왔다. 나를 믿는 사람은 누구나 어둠 속에 머물지 않게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 나는 빛으로 세상에 왔다. 나를 믿는 사람은 누구든지 어둠 속에 머물지 않게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 빛으로 이 세상에 왔다. 나를 믿는 사람들이 어둠 속에 남아 있지 않게 하려고 온 것이다.

pt.L: Eu vim ao mundo [como] luz, para que todo aquele que crê em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não permaneça nas trevas.
pt.B: Eu vim ao mundo como luz, para que quem crê em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não permaneça nas trevas.
pt.R: Eu vim ao mundo como uma luz. Vim para que as pessoas que acreditam em {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} não fiquem no escuro.

decisions.choice: I have come into the world as light: Jesus brings God's light to humanity
decisions.reason: "I" is stated for emphasis and "light" stands first in the sentence. The saying takes up the prologue (the true light coming into the world, 1:9), 3:19 ("the light has come into the world"), 8:12 and 9:5, and the call of 12:35-36 to believe in the light while it is still here.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity, living in darkness
decisions.reason: Key term. As in 1:9-10 and 3:19, the world is the human race, into which the light comes because it lies in darkness.

decisions.choice: remain in the darkness: stay where all people are without him
decisions.reason: "Remain" assumes that people are already in the darkness, the condition of life without God (1:5; 8:12; 12:35). Believing in Jesus brings them out of it. The same verb says that God's wrath "remains" on the one who refuses the Son (3:36), and that sin "remains" for those who claim to see (9:41).

decisions.choice: as a light (B, R); whoever believes (B), people who believe (R); I came so that (R)
decisions.reason: "Whoever" and "people who" give the sense of "everyone who" with the negative on the verb, as English puts it. Readable starts a new sentence for the purpose and repeats "I came".

decisions.choice: stay in the dark
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for this verb is "remain"; Readable uses the everyday "stay", which young readers know better, and "the dark".

decisions.choice: no se quede (B, R); no permanezca (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the book-wide verb; Balanced and Readable use the everyday one for staying where one is (meaning decision m3).

source.text: καὶ ἐάν τίς μου ἀκούσῃ τῶν ῥημάτων καὶ μὴ φυλάξῃ, ἐγὼ οὐ κρίνω αὐτόν, οὐ γὰρ ἦλθον ἵνα κρίνω τὸν κόσμον ἀλλ’ ἵνα σώσω τὸν κόσμον.

records.literal_gloss: And if anyone of me hears the words and not keeps, I not judge him; not for I came so that I might judge the world but so that I might save the world.

en.L: And if anyone hears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words and does not keep [them], I do not judge {{gender:them|him}}; for I did not come to judge the world but to save the world.
en.B: If anyone hears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words but does not keep them, I do not condemn {{gender:them|him}}. For I did not come to condemn the world, but to save the world.
en.R: If people hear what I say but do not obey it, I do not judge them guilty. I did not come to judge the world guilty. I came to save the world.

es.L: Y si alguno oye {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras y no las guarda, yo no lo juzgo; porque no vine a juzgar al mundo, sino a salvar al mundo.
es.B: Si alguno oye {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras pero no las cumple, yo no lo condeno. Porque no vine a condenar al mundo, sino a salvar al mundo.
es.R: Si alguien oye lo que digo pero no lo obedece, yo no lo declaro culpable. No vine a declarar culpable al mundo. Vine a salvar al mundo.

fr.L: Et si quelqu’un entend {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles et ne [les] garde pas, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je ne le juge pas ; car je ne suis pas venu pour juger le monde, mais pour sauver le monde.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un entend {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles mais ne les garde pas, ce n’est pas {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui le condamne. Car je ne suis pas venu condamner le monde, mais sauver le monde.
fr.R: Si des gens entendent ce que je dis mais n’y obéissent pas, ce n’est pas {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui les déclare coupables. Je ne suis pas venu déclarer le monde coupable. Je suis venu sauver le monde.

sw.L: Na mtu akiyasikia maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} wala asiyashike, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} simhukumu; kwa maana sikuja ili niuhukumu ulimwengu, bali niuokoe ulimwengu.
sw.B: Mtu akiyasikia maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} lakini asiyashike, simhukumu. Kwa maana sikuja kuuhukumu ulimwengu, bali kuuokoa ulimwengu.
sw.R: Watu wakisikia ninachosema lakini wasikitii, siwahukumu kuwa na hatia. Sikuja kuuhukumu ulimwengu kuwa na hatia. Nilikuja kuuokoa ulimwengu.

vi.L: Và nếu ai nghe những lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà không giữ [lấy], {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không xét đoán người ấy; vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã không đến để xét đoán thế gian, mà để cứu thế gian.
vi.B: Nếu ai nghe lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà không vâng giữ, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không kết án người ấy. Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến không phải để kết án thế gian, mà để cứu thế gian.
vi.R: Nếu ai nghe lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà không vâng theo, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không kết tội người ấy. Ta đến không phải để kết tội thế gian. Ta đến để cứu thế gian.

ko.L: 누가 내 말을 듣고도 지키지 않더라도, 나는 그 사람을 심판하지 않는다. 나는 세상을 심판하러 온 것이 아니라 세상을 구원하러 왔기 때문이다.
ko.B: 누구든지 내 말을 듣고도 지키지 않으면, 나는 그 사람을 정죄하지 않는다. 나는 세상을 정죄하러 온 것이 아니라 세상을 구원하러 왔기 때문이다.
ko.R: 사람들이 내 말을 듣고도 따르지 않아도, 나는 그들에게 죄가 있다고 판결하지 않는다. 나는 세상을 심판하러 온 것이 아니다. 세상을 구원하러 왔다.

pt.L: E, se alguém ouve as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras e não [as] guarda, eu não o julgo; pois não vim para julgar o mundo, mas para salvar o mundo.
pt.B: Se alguém ouve as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras, mas não as guarda, eu não o condeno. Pois eu não vim para condenar o mundo, mas para salvar o mundo.
pt.R: Se as pessoas ouvem o que eu digo, mas não obedecem, eu não as condeno. Eu não vim para condenar o mundo. Eu vim para salvar o mundo.

decisions.choice: keep: hold to and obey
decisions.reason: The verb means to guard or keep safe; with words or commands it means to hold to them and do them. Jesus uses another verb for the same thing in 8:51 and 14:23.

decisions.choice: judge: condemn
decisions.reason: Set against "save", the verb means a judgment that goes against someone, as in 3:17, which this sentence echoes. The Son has authority to judge (5:22, 27), but condemning is not the purpose of his coming (8:15).

decisions.choice: I do not judge him: it is not Jesus himself who condemns; his word will (12:48)
decisions.reason: The "I" is stated for emphasis and prepares for the next verse, where the word he has spoken is the judge.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity, as in 3:17
decisions.reason: Key term. Jesus came for the human race as a whole, the world God loves (3:16).

decisions.choice: condemn (B); judge ... guilty (R)
decisions.reason: As in 3:17: Literal keeps "judge" so that the word family of 12:47-48 can be seen; Balanced and Readable give its sense here (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}} (L, B); people ... them (R)
decisions.reason: "Anyone" means a man or a woman, so the pronoun after it takes the gender setting. Readable uses a plural, which needs none, and says "obey" for "keep" (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: condeno (B); declaro culpable (R); juzgo (L)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Lo" is a clitic, and Spanish needs no other pronoun here. Literal's "las" is required by Spanish, so it is not bracketed.

decisions.choice: "quelqu’un ... le" with no gender setting (also "celui qui ... le" in 12:48)
alternatives: gender setting spans offering "le ou la", as the English offers "them" and "him"
decisions.reason: English needs the gender setting for "them|him" after "anyone". French takes up "quelqu’un" and "celui qui" with the generic masculine "le", which grammar requires here, as after "chacun" and "personne", which the French brief (§7) counts as already inclusive; a doubled "le ou la" would weigh down a short saying. Readable uses a plural, as the English does. A native reviewer may prefer spans.

decisions.choice: ce n’est pas moi qui le condamne (B); moi, je ne le juge pas (L)
decisions.reason: "I" is stated for emphasis and prepares for 12:48, where his word is the judge (meaning decision m3). French shows the emphasis with "moi" (Literal) or "ce n’est pas moi qui" (Balanced, Readable).

decisions.choice: eu não o julgo / condeno, with no gender setting
alternatives: {{gender:eu não a julgo|eu não o julgo}}
decisions.reason: The English puts "them/him" under the gender setting. In Portuguese the "o" that refers back to "alguém" is the ordinary generic pronoun and already includes women (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7); the same holds for "o julgue", "julgá-lo" in 12:48.

decisions.choice: condeno, condenar (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "condenar", the plain Portuguese word for a judgment that goes against someone (meaning decision m2), where the English Readable needs "judge ... guilty".

source.text: ὁ ἀθετῶν ἐμὲ καὶ μὴ λαμβάνων τὰ ῥήματά μου ἔχει τὸν κρίνοντα αὐτόν· ὁ λόγος ὃν ἐλάλησα ἐκεῖνος κρινεῖ αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ·

records.literal_gloss: The [one] rejecting me and not receiving the words of me has the [one] judging him; the word which I spoke, that will judge him in the last day;

en.L: The one who rejects {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and does not receive {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words has one who judges {{gender:them|him}}: the word that I spoke, that will judge {{gender:them|him}} on the last day.
en.B: Anyone who rejects {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and does not accept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words has a judge: the very word I have spoken will judge {{gender:them|him}} on the last day.
en.R: People who reject {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and do not accept what I say will have a judge. On the last day, the message I have given will be their judge.

es.L: El que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rechaza y no recibe {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras tiene quien lo juzgue: la palabra que he hablado, esa lo juzgará en el último día.
es.B: El que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rechaza y no acepta {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras tiene un juez: la misma palabra que he hablado lo juzgará en el último día.
es.R: Los que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rechazan y no aceptan lo que digo tendrán un juez. En el último día, el mensaje que les he dado será su juez.

fr.L: Celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejette et ne reçoit pas {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles a celui qui le juge : la parole que j’ai prononcée, celle-là le jugera au dernier jour.
fr.B: Celui qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejette et n’accepte pas {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} paroles a un juge : la parole même que j’ai prononcée le jugera au dernier jour.
fr.R: Les gens qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejettent et n’acceptent pas ce que je dis auront un juge. Au dernier jour, le message que je leur ai donné sera leur juge.

sw.L: Anayenikataa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} na asiyeyapokea maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} anaye wa kumhukumu: neno nililolisema, hilo ndilo litakalomhukumu siku ya mwisho.
sw.B: Yeyote anayenikataa na asiyeyakubali maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ana mwamuzi: neno lile lile nililolisema litamhukumu siku ya mwisho.
sw.R: Watu wanaonikataa na wasiokubali ninachosema watakuwa na mwamuzi. Siku ya mwisho, ujumbe nilioutoa ndio utakaowahukumu.

vi.L: Người khước từ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và không nhận lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì đã có điều xét đoán người ấy: lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói, chính lời ấy sẽ xét đoán người ấy trong ngày sau cùng.
vi.B: Ai khước từ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và không nhận lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì đã có một quan tòa: chính lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói sẽ xét xử người ấy vào ngày sau cùng.
vi.R: Ai từ chối {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và không nhận lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì sẽ có một quan tòa. Vào ngày sau cùng, chính sứ điệp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền ra sẽ xét xử người ấy.

ko.L: 나를 저버리고 내 말을 받아들이지 않는 사람에게는 그를 심판하는 이가 있다. 내가 한 그 말이 마지막 날에 그를 심판할 것이다.
ko.B: 나를 거부하고 내 말을 받아들이지 않는 사람에게는 심판자가 있다. 바로 내가 한 말이 마지막 날에 그 사람을 심판할 것이다.
ko.R: 나를 거부하고 내 말을 받아들이지 않는 사람들에게는 심판자가 있을 것이다. 마지막 날에 내가 전한 말이 그들을 심판할 것이다.

pt.L: Quem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejeita e não recebe as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras tem quem o julgue: a palavra que eu falei, essa o julgará no último dia.
pt.B: Quem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejeita e não aceita as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras tem um juiz: a própria palavra que eu falei vai julgá-lo no último dia.
pt.R: As pessoas que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rejeitam e não aceitam o que eu digo vão ter um juiz. No último dia, a mensagem que eu dei vai ser o juiz delas.

decisions.choice: rejects: sets aside, refuses; receive: accept and take in
decisions.reason: The first verb means to set something aside as worthless (Luke 10:16 uses it of rejecting Jesus and the one who sent him). Not receiving his words is the opposite of keeping them (12:47) and of receiving him (1:12).

decisions.choice: has one who judges him: the word he has spoken, that word and no other
decisions.reason: The first half leaves the judge unnamed; the second names it. "That" picks up "the word" with emphasis. So 12:47 and 12:48 agree: Jesus does not come to condemn, but the one who refuses his word is not left without a judge. The word is the message Jesus has spoken, which is the Father's own (12:49).

decisions.choice: the last day: the day of resurrection and judgment
decisions.reason: John speaks of "the last day" as the day when Jesus raises those who believe (6:39-40, 44, 54; 11:24). Judgment is already at work now (3:18-19; 5:24), and it will be completed on that day, when the word people refused will stand against them. The Son is the judge (5:22, 27); here it is his word that judges, since he judges by what he hears from the Father (5:30).

decisions.choice: a judge; the very word (B); the message I have given (R)
decisions.reason: "Has a judge" is the natural English for "has the one judging him". "The very word" carries the emphatic "that" (meaning decision m2). Readable says "message", since "word" here is everything Jesus has said.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}} (L, B); People ... their (R)
decisions.reason: "The one who rejects" means anyone, man or woman, so the pronoun takes the gender setting. Readable uses a plural, which needs none.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: As in verse 47: "lo" is a clitic.

decisions.choice: un juez; la misma palabra (B); el mensaje que les he dado (R)
decisions.reason: As in English.

source.text: ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐξ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐκ ἐλάλησα, ἀλλ’ ὁ πέμψας με πατὴρ αὐτός μοι ἐντολὴν δέδωκεν τί εἴπω καὶ τί λαλήσω.

records.literal_gloss: Because I from myself not spoke, but the having sent me Father, he me a commandment has given what I may say and what I may speak.

en.L: For I did not speak from {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, but the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak.
en.B: For I have not spoken on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own authority; the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a commandment about what to say and what to speak.
en.R: I have not spoken just on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own. The Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a command about everything I should say.

es.L: Porque yo no he hablado por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo, sino que el Padre que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dado mandamiento de lo que he de decir y de lo que he de hablar.
es.B: Porque no he hablado por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} propia autoridad. El Padre que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dado el mandamiento de lo que debo decir y hablar.
es.R: No he hablado solo por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cuenta. El Padre que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mandó todo lo que debo decir.

fr.L: Car je n’ai pas parlé de {{deity_pronoun:moi-même|Moi-même}}, mais le Père qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} donné un commandement : ce que je dois dire et ce que je dois prononcer.
fr.B: Car je n’ai pas parlé de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} propre autorité ; le Père qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} commandé ce que je dois dire et annoncer.
fr.R: Je n’ai pas parlé de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} propre initiative. Le Père qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} commandé tout ce que je devais dire.

sw.L: Kwa maana sikusema kwa nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, bali Baba aliyenituma {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} amenipa amri, nitakaloliseme na nitakaloliongea.
sw.B: Kwa maana sikusema kwa mamlaka {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}; Baba aliyenituma {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} amenipa amri juu ya nitakalosema na nitakaloongea.
sw.R: Sikusema kwa nia {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} tu. Baba aliyenituma {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alinipa amri juu ya kila kitu ninachopaswa kusema.

vi.L: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không tự mình nói ra, nhưng Cha, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ban cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} điều răn: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phải nói gì và phải truyền gì.
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không nói theo ý riêng mình; chính Cha, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đã truyền lệnh cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} về những gì phải nói và phải truyền dạy.
vi.R: Ta không tự ý nói ra những điều này. Chính Cha, Đấng đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đã truyền lệnh cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} về mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phải nói.

ko.L: 나는 나 스스로 말하지 않았고, 나를 보내신 아버지께서 친히 내가 무엇을 말하고 무엇을 이야기할지 내게 명령을 주셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 나는 내 권한으로 말하지 않았다. 나를 보내신 아버지께서 친히 내가 무엇을 말하고 무엇을 전할지 명령해 주셨다.
ko.R: 나는 내 생각대로 말하지 않았다. 나를 보내신 아버지께서 친히 내가 할 말을 모두 명령해 주셨다.

pt.L: Porque eu não falei por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} mesmo, mas o Pai que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} mesmo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deu um mandamento: o que devo dizer e o que devo falar.
pt.B: Pois eu não falei por {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} própria autoridade: o Pai que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou é quem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deu um mandamento sobre o que dizer e o que falar.
pt.R: Eu não falei só por {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} conta. O próprio Pai, que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} enviou, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deu uma ordem sobre tudo o que eu devo dizer.

decisions.choice: for: the reason the word will judge (12:48)
decisions.reason: The word Jesus has spoken will judge because it is not his own private word but the word the Father gave him. To refuse it is to refuse God.

decisions.choice: from myself: on my own authority, apart from the Father
decisions.reason: As in 5:19, 30, 7:17-18 and 14:10, the phrase means acting or speaking on one's own initiative. Jesus never speaks as a separate voice from the Father.

decisions.choice: a commandment: a charge given by the Father; what to say and what to speak: all that he says
alternatives: "say" for the content and "speak" for the manner of saying it
decisions.reason: The commandment is the Father's charge to the Son about his message (compare 10:18 and 14:31). The two verbs for speaking are close in meaning and together cover everything he has said. Some take the first as what he says and the second as how he says it; the text does not press the difference.

decisions.choice: the prophet like Moses: Deuteronomy 18:18-19
decisions.reason: God promised to raise up a prophet like Moses: "I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I command him", and whoever does not listen to those words will answer to God (Deuteronomy 18:18-19). Jesus's words in 12:48-49 follow the same order: he speaks only what the Father commands, and refusing his words brings judgment. The crowds had wondered whether he was "the prophet" (6:14; 7:40).

decisions.choice: on my own authority (B); just on my own (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:19 and 5:30, which say "on my own"; Balanced adds "authority" here because Jesus speaks under a commission (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: a command about everything I should say
alternatives: a commandment, what to say and what to speak
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two near-synonyms into one phrase (meaning decision m3), since "what to say and what to speak" sounds like a repetition in English.

decisions.choice: por mi propia autoridad (B); solo por mi cuenta (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo, for the Father
decisions.reason: The stressed "él" for the Father takes the setting.

decisions.choice: "điều răn" (L, and "điều răn" in 12:50 L, B); "truyền lệnh" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "điều răn" is the Bible word for a commandment of God; Balanced and Readable turn the noun into the verb "truyền lệnh" where that reads more naturally.

source.text: καὶ οἶδα ὅτι ἡ ἐντολὴ αὐτοῦ ζωὴ αἰώνιός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: And I know that the commandment of him life eternal is.

en.L: And I know that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandment is eternal life.
en.B: And I know that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandment is eternal life.
en.R: And I know that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} command gives eternal life, the life of the age to come, which starts now.

es.L: Y sé que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mandamiento es vida eterna.
es.B: Y sé que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mandamiento es vida eterna.
es.R: Y sé que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mandato da vida eterna, la vida del mundo venidero, que comienza ya.

fr.L: Et je sais que {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} commandement est [la] vie éternelle.
fr.B: Et je sais que {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} commandement est la vie éternelle.
fr.R: Et je sais que ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commande donne la vie éternelle, la vie du monde à venir, qui commence dès maintenant.

sw.L: Nami najua kwamba agizo {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni uzima wa milele.
sw.B: Nami najua kwamba amri {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ni uzima wa milele.
sw.R: Nami najua kwamba amri {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} inaleta uzima wa milele, uzima wa nyakati zijazo, unaoanza sasa.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết rằng điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là sự sống đời đời.
vi.B: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết rằng điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là sự sống đời đời.
vi.R: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết rằng mệnh lệnh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban sự sống đời đời, là sự sống của thời đại sắp đến, bắt đầu ngay từ bây giờ.

ko.L: 그리고 나는 그분의 명령이 영원한 생명이라는 것을 안다.
ko.B: 나는 그분의 명령이 영원한 생명이라는 것을 안다.
ko.R: 나는 그분의 명령이 영원한 생명을 준다는 것을 안다. 영원한 생명은 오는 세상의 생명인데, 지금 이미 시작된다.

pt.L: E eu sei que o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} mandamento é vida eterna.
pt.B: E eu sei que o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} mandamento é vida eterna.
pt.R: E eu sei que a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ordem dá a vida eterna, a vida do tempo que está por vir, e que começa agora.

decisions.choice: his commandment is eternal life: it leads to and gives eternal life
alternatives: the command and eternal life are one and the same thing
decisions.reason: The Father's charge to the Son is to speak his words, and those words give life to those who receive them: "the words I have spoken to you are spirit and life" (6:63); Peter says Jesus has "words of eternal life" (6:68). Moses said of God's commands, "it is your life" (Deuteronomy 32:47; compare 30:15-20).

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of the age to come, given now
decisions.reason: Key term. Eternal life is knowing the Father and the one he sent (17:3), and the one who believes has it already (5:24). After the warning of judgment in 12:48, Jesus's last public words end on life, the purpose for which the Father sent him (3:16).

decisions.choice: gives eternal life, the life of the age to come, which starts now
decisions.reason: Readable says how the command "is" life (meaning decision m1) and explains "eternal life" once in the passage, as the book's terms allow.

decisions.choice: da vida eterna, la vida del mundo venidero, que comienza ya
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ἃ οὖν ἐγὼ λαλῶ, καθὼς εἴρηκέν μοι ὁ πατήρ, οὕτως λαλῶ.

records.literal_gloss: What therefore I speak, just as has said to me the Father, so I speak."

en.L: So what I speak, just as the Father has told {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so I speak."
en.B: So whatever I say, I say just as the Father has told {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: So everything I say is just what the Father has told {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to say."

es.L: Así que lo que yo hablo, tal como el Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} lo ha dicho, así lo hablo».
es.B: Así que todo lo que digo, lo digo tal como el Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} lo ha dicho».
es.R: Así que todo lo que digo es exactamente lo que el Padre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha dicho que diga».

fr.L: Ce que je dis donc, comme le Père {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} l’a dit, ainsi je [le] dis. »
fr.B: Ainsi, tout ce que je dis, je le dis comme le Père {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} l’a dit. »
fr.R: Donc tout ce que je dis, c’est exactement ce que le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a dit de dire. »

sw.L: Basi ninayoyasema, kama vile Baba alivyoniambia, ndivyo ninavyoyasema."
sw.B: Kwa hiyo chochote ninachosema, nakisema kama vile Baba alivyoniambia."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo kila kitu ninachosema ni kile hasa ambacho Baba ameniambia niseme."

vi.L: Vậy, điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói, Cha đã bảo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thế nào, thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói thế ấy."
vi.B: Vậy, bất cứ điều gì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đều nói đúng như Cha đã bảo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Vậy mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói đều đúng như những gì Cha đã bảo {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói."

ko.L: 그러므로 내가 말하는 것은, 아버지께서 내게 말씀하신 그대로 그렇게 말하는 것이다."
ko.B: 그러므로 무엇을 말하든지, 나는 아버지께서 내게 말씀하신 그대로 말한다."
ko.R: 그래서 내가 하는 말은 모두 아버지께서 내게 하라고 하신 그대로이다."

pt.L: Assim, o que eu falo, conforme o Pai {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} disse, assim eu falo."
pt.B: Por isso, tudo o que eu digo, digo exatamente como o Pai {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} falou."
pt.R: Por isso, tudo o que eu digo é exatamente o que o Pai {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mandou dizer."

decisions.choice: so ... just as ... so: what he says matches exactly what the Father has said to him
decisions.reason: "So" draws the conclusion from 12:49-50a: because the Father's command gives life, Jesus speaks exactly as he has been told. "Has told" is in a tense of lasting result: the Father's word to him stands. The same pattern of "just as ... so" is used in 8:28 and 14:31.

decisions.choice: whatever I say, I say just as (B); everything I say is just what ... to say (R)
alternatives: what I speak, just as the Father has told me, so I speak (Literal)
decisions.reason: English does not place a "just as" clause between the object and its verb. Balanced and Readable reorder the sentence; Literal keeps the Greek order.

decisions.choice: todo lo que digo, lo digo tal como (B); es exactamente lo que ... que diga (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m1).
